summary:
OptiMoon is a lunar mission-planning project developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge Lunar Landing Site Navigator. It provides an interactive decision-support framework for evaluating and comparing lunar landing sites and mission windows using historical mission data, landing coordinates, topographic information and astronomical ephemerides.

The platform assesses four key parameters: solar elevation angle, sunlight duration, Earth visibility and temperature range. These factors are integrated into a multi-criteria methodology that calculates an Optimal Landing Score, enabling objective comparison of candidate landing locations and dates.

By combining astronomical, environmental and operational data into accessible indicators, OptiMoon helps address the challenge of identifying favourable lunar landing opportunities. The approach is particularly relevant to the Lunar South Polar Region, where illumination conditions, communication opportunities, thermal constraints and terrain characteristics strongly influence mission feasibility.

The project combines scientific datasets, environmental analysis and interactive visualization to support informed decision-making for future robotic and human lunar missions. Ultimately, OptiMoon aims to bridge the gap between scientific data and mission design, contributing to safer, more efficient and sustainable lunar exploration while supporting the long-term goal of establishing a permanent human presence on the Moon.
details:
OptiMoon is a lunar mission-planning and landing-site assessment platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its objective is to support the identification and comparison of suitable lunar landing locations and mission windows by integrating historical mission data, astronomical calculations and environmental metrics into a unified decision-support framework.

The project addresses a fundamental challenge in lunar exploration: landing-site suitability cannot be determined solely by geographic location. Illumination conditions, communication opportunities, thermal constraints and local topography all play critical roles in mission success. OptiMoon therefore adopts a multi-criteria assessment approach, with particular focus on the Lunar South Polar Region, a strategically important area for future robotic and human exploration.

The platform is built on a structured database of historical, ongoing and planned lunar missions, including landing locations, coordinates, mission dates and mission characteristics. This dataset provides a reference framework for analyzing exploration trends and comparing candidate landing sites. Environmental and topographic information is enriched using altitude data derived from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) QuickMap resources.

Four key parameters form the foundation of the landing-site assessment methodology: solar elevation angle, sunlight duration, Earth visibility and temperature range. Solar elevation and sunlight duration provide indicators of illumination conditions and solar-power potential. Earth visibility estimates direct communication opportunities, while temperature range helps identify thermal challenges that may affect mission operations. Surface altitude and local terrain characteristics are also considered to evaluate potential topographic obstructions and improve overall site characterization.

A central feature of OptiMoon is the Optimal Landing Score, a composite metric designed to compare candidate sites using a consistent set of environmental and operational criteria. Rather than evaluating locations independently, the framework enables users to explore trade-offs between illumination, communications, thermal stability and geographical conditions. The resulting score provides a comparative assessment of site suitability to support mission-planning decisions.

The project combines publicly available scientific datasets, astronomical modelling and data analytics. LROC QuickMap provides essential lunar reference data. Looker Studio enables interactive visualization and exploration of mission and environmental datasets and Google Sites delivers a centralized web platform where users can access project information and analytical reports. As a software-based decision-support system, OptiMoon does not require dedicated hardware.

The innovative aspect of OptiMoon lies in its ability to integrate multiple sources of lunar information into a practical mission-planning environment. Rather than functioning as a static catalogue of landing sites, the platform supports dynamic, multi-parameter assessment of candidate locations by combining environmental, operational, geographical and temporal factors within a single analytical framework.

Ultimately, OptiMoon aims to contribute to safer, more informed and more efficient lunar mission planning. By making complex scientific information easier to analyze and compare, the platform can help mission designers, researchers and exploration organizations identify promising landing opportunities and better understand the trade-offs involved in site selection. In doing so, OptiMoon supports the broader vision of sustainable lunar exploration and the long-term establishment of a permanent human presence on the Moon.
